stories.title: Michigan Democrats prepare for a second trifecta
stories.summary: Michigan Democrats secured a legislative trifecta, regaining full control of the state House and Senate, along with the governor's office. House Minority Leader Ranjeev Puri (D-Canton) is expected to continue leading House Democrats, with the party holding more than a one-vote majority in the upcoming session.

inputFacts.title: Michigan Democrats prepare for a second trifecta
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Democrats have regained full control of the state Legislature and governor’s office following election night wins, expanding their Senate majority and flipping multiple House seats. The party aims to advance policies like gun safety and clean energy with a stronger majority, learning from their previous trifecta period. Leadership transitions and new members will shape the upcoming legislative session.

inputFacts.title: What Michigan election results mean for data centers, DTE, clean energy
inputFacts.summary: Democrats retained control of Michigan's governor's office and state Senate while gaining the House majority, enabling potential advancements in clean energy and environmental protections. The Michiganders for Money Out of Politics ballot initiative banning utility political spending passed with 81% support, while a constitutional convention measure failed. Abdul El-Sayed's Senate victory could influence federal data center regulations, and new leaders like Eli Savit pledged to continue utility ratepayer advocacy. Ballot initiatives like Proposal 2 and Ann Arbor's Proposition E had mixed outcomes, with the latter failing to establish a municipal energy utility.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor school board to welcome four new trustees
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor Board of Education will see one incumbent and four new trustees take office in January after this week’s election. WEMU’s Kevin Meerschaert reported on the changes.

inputFacts.title: Cinema Chat: 'Godzilla Minus Zero,' 'Wild Horse Nine,' 'Chronovisor' open this weekend
inputFacts.summary: WEMU's Mat Hopson and Tara Calligan discussed new sci-fi films arriving in downtown Ann Arbor's movie theaters, including 'Godzilla Minus Zero,' 'Wild Horse Nine,' and 'Chronovisor.'

inputFacts.title: Navigating AI in transportation: New national research consortium aims to guide agencies
inputFacts.summary: Three leading transportation research institutes are forming the National AI Consortium for Transportation (NAICT) to provide agencies with a non-commercial resource for evaluating, deploying, and governing AI. The consortium includes the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute, UC Berkeley Institute of Transportation Studies, and Texas A&M Transportation Institute. Initial activities include listening sessions and workshops to align priorities with agencies and develop educational resources and governance frameworks for AI in transportation.

inputFacts.title: Supporters of Ypsilanti's Proposal B say it will survive any legal challenge
inputFacts.summary: Supporters of Ypsilanti's Proposal B, a recent ballot initiative, expressed confidence that the proposal will withstand potential legal challenges following its passage.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor voters reject Proposal E
inputFacts.summary: Voters in Ann Arbor rejected Proposal E, which aimed to explore replacing DTE Energy as the city's main electric provider. The measure failed by 951 votes. City council members opposed the proposal, citing legal risks and potential costs, while advocates argued for public power alternatives.
